column12: it leans HIGH, in four named ways. The age share is 5 to 11 and the trial takes 6 to 11. The control shares are measured on 5 to 17 year olds and applied to the younger band. column12: two mismatches, and the published paediatric evidence says the row errs low. It is a Medicare population where the layer is children aged 6 to 11, the same mismatch the price row carries, and it is a prevalent stock rather than a cohort of starters. Averell CM, Laliberte F, Germain G, Slade DJ, Duh MS, Spahn J, 'Disease burden and treatment adherence among children and adolescent patients with asthma', J Asthma 2022;59(8):1687-1696 (doi 10.1080/02770903.2021.1955377, PMID 34346263), IQVIA PharMetrics Plus, 10,247 US patients aged 5 to 17 initiating a twice-daily inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta agonist: 'Persistence with twice-daily ICS and ICS/LABA was 10.1% and 14.2% at 6 months; 5.6% and 8.0% at 12 months', persistence being no gap over 45 days, so 92.0% of starters stop within a year on that definition. The CMS rate is taken because it is measured on the beneficiaries the price is quoted on, which is what makes the stock times the price reproduce the file's own spend, and because a 12-month figure on starters counts front-loaded dropout a prevalent stock has already survived. A reviewer who prefers the population match to the price match should take 0.92 and carry the published definition with it
